content.text: Decision guide · 2026 data · [EM-VERIFIED] Repair vs Replacement Engine Cost Decision Guide UK 2026 Repair costs: £50-£2,000+ · Replacement (reconditioned): £2,000-£6,000+ The real question is not price - it's: "Are you fixing one failure, or eliminating the risk of another within 12 months-" Repair £50-£2,000+ 3-12 months warranty · 1-5 days off-road Replacement (reconditioned) £2,000-£6,000+ 6-24 months warranty · 3-7 days off-road Get accurate pricing in 60s → 100+ UK specialist suppliers 24,650 verified quotes in 2025 No obligation · Free 🔒 Secure enquiry · no spam · genuine quotes from vetted UK engine suppliers. About this data · our methodology This guide is based on 24,650 real engine replacement quote requests submitted through Engines Market between January and December 2025. Every quote comes from a real UK vehicle owner; suppliers respond with real quoted prices. All figures are anonymised and aggregated. Repair cost estimates are derived from industry workshop data and supplier interviews. It does not address hidden wear on other components. Timing chain replacement - £650-£1,800 fixes the chain. But the turbo, injectors, and oil pump remain at 100k+ miles, ready to fail. Head gasket repair - £1,000-£2,500 fixes the gasket. But the bottom end has unknown bearing wear. Turbo replacement - £800-£2,500 fixes the turbo. But the engine may have suffered oil contamination during the failure. "In real UK workshop practice, repair addresses only the visible failure. Replacement eliminates all variables. The 50% rule is the dominant decision logic in the UK engine industry: if repair exceeds 50% of replacement cost, replacement is better value - particularly for vehicles worth £4,000-£15,000 and kept 2+ years."
